newsitem.title: USA: US High Court rejects state law on spouse pension.
newsitem.headline: US High Court rejects state law on spouse pension.

text.p: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled Monday that federal pension law takes precedence over any state law that might give spouses an automatic share in each other's pension plans.

The High Court, by a 5-4 vote, said the federal Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 pre-empts a Lousiana law that allows a spouse to transfer his or her interest in undistributed pension plan benefits.

"Given the pervasive significance of pension plans in the national economy, the congressional mandate for their uniform and comprehensive regulation and the fundamental importance of community property law in defining the marital partnership in a number of states, the question is of undoubted importance," Justice Anthony Kennedy said for the court in the ruling.

The case involved the application of Louisiana's community property law to a pension annuity a retired worker's second wife received after his death in 1989. His first wife, who died in 1979, had left most of her estate to their three sons.
The sons claimed they were entitled to the pension because it was part of their late mother's community property that belonged to her estate.

But the Supreme Court disagreed and sided with the second wife, who argued federal law takes precedence over any state community property laws. She said she was entitled to continue receiving the pension as the surviving spouse.
The decision was a victory for the U.S. Justice Department, which argued on behalf of the Labor Department that federal law should continue to take precedence over any competing state measures.
